source.title: Trade-offs between membership privacy&adversarially robust learning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests how adversarial training and training-set size relate to overfitting on Gaussian data and image-classification benchmarks, extending the claim's generalization-gap subject to robust training.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization or any listed V1–V8 version. It reports its own training/test loss gaps, membership-attack accuracy, and test accuracy under standard and adversarial training. Figure values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text. Cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests how adversarial training and dataset size affect loss gaps and membership privacy, not any V1–V8 version. Section 3 invokes Feldman and Zhang's removal results to justify an assumption about individual examples' influence; it supplies no independent V8 test. Appendix C.2 studies partially corrupted Gaussian labels, not V1's fixed random-label memorization comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that robust training can produce either more or less overfitting and membership vulnerability than standard training, depending on training-set size and perturbation strength, with related empirical patterns on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The theoretical privacy interpretation depends on their membership-inference assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: Studies adversarial versus standard training and loss-gap/membership outcomes, rather than random-label fitting or the interventions and measures in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The loss gap and membership-attack accuracy vary with training-set size and adversarial perturbation strength; on CIFAR-10, results also vary with training method (standard, FGSM, PGD).

fits_no_version.finding: Gaussian analysis and CIFAR experiments show that adversarial training can increase or decrease loss gaps and membership vulnerability depending on training-set size and perturbation strength.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial training's effect on overfitting and membership privacy depends on dataset size and perturbation strength.

fits_no_version.finding: The Gaussian experiments report zero average classification error for n greater than 2 despite a nonzero training–test loss gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low classification error can coexist with a nonzero training–test loss gap.

record.problems: The Gaussian analysis uses a simple binary classification model and linear loss. The image experiments use a particular ResNet-18 setup and training recipe. The authors describe some CIFAR cases where larger loss gaps correspond to smaller membership accuracy and attribute this mainly to weak membership attacks. Plotted results do not provide recoverable numerical values in the supplied text; repetitions are reported without error bars.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results on the claim versions were omitted. The paper's appendix plots for intermediate training epochs are not separately extracted because their individual values are figure-only and the text summarizes the relevant loss-gap and membership trends in R5–R8.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width increases beyond zero training error and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, gap rankings, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples; only prior results are invoked.

record.verdict_notes: T6 is relative to the specified versions, despite the study's substantive results about generalization and privacy. All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a listed effect; this does not dispute the reported effects themselves. The V8 citation is used to motivate an assumption, not offered as an independent removal experiment or a direct challenge to V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: linear classifier on binary Gaussian data
rows.size_stated: 100d for the plotted example; other dimensions not stated
rows.operation_detail: Adversarial training with perturbation ε varied; theoretical expected training–test loss gap across training-set sizes.

conditions.value: binary Gaussian; μ=σ=1 in plotted example

rows.baseline: Standard-training loss gap at the same training-set size
rows.value: For ε=μ² and ε=μ, the plotted gap is larger than with standard training; for ε=2μ and ε=4μ, it is smaller. The paper states that ε=2μ gives a smaller gap for every n.
rows.note: The direction depends on perturbation and training-set size; plotted values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: No listed version is measured. The theoretical result has no 200-epoch training stage. Distinguish a smaller signed gap from a smaller absolute gap: for epsilon greater than 2 mu, the gap can become negative, which still permits membership leakage. The extracted epsilon notation is ambiguous in the supplied typeset text.

rows.subject: linear classifier on binary Gaussian data

rows.baseline: Standard training for the corresponding training-set size
rows.value: Average empirical findings closely match the expected decrease in loss gaps; robust models can have a smaller gap than standard models for some ε and n.
rows.uncertainty: Averaged over 10 repetitions; no error bars stated.
rows.note: The paper describes the plotted trends; individual values are figure-only.
rows.check: Empirical loss-gap agreement with the Gaussian theory does not measure any listed version. The intermediate epsilon notation cannot be resolved confidently from the supplied text.

rows.subject: linear classifier on binary Gaussian data
rows.operation_detail: Standard and robust training; test accuracy measured as training-set size increases.
rows.value: Average generalization error fell to zero if n>2 for both standard and robust training.
rows.uncertainty: Averaged over 10 repetitions in the described experiments; no error bars stated.
rows.note: The paper reports zero generalization error alongside a nonzero loss gap.
rows.check: The reported empirical zero classification error does not establish V1 without random-label fitting and evaluation. Preserve it as an empirical report, not a theorem of exactly zero population error.
